subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill.

hook.text: On April 20, 2010, the Deepwater Horizon rig exploded, killing 11 workers and spilling 4.9 million barrels of oil.

buildup.text: The well was drilled 5,000 feet underwater into rock 13,000 feet below the seabed. Extreme depth created extreme pressures.

discovery.text: A cement seal at the bottom of the well failed. High-pressure gas shot up the pipe and ignited on the platform.

twist.text: The blowout preventer — the last line of defense — had a dead battery and a faulty ram. It didn't activate.

climax.text: It took 87 days to cap the well. BP paid $65 billion in cleanup costs, fines, and legal settlements.

punchline.text: Bad cement. Dead battery. 87 days of uncontrolled oil.

quiz.question: Why did the blowout preventer fail during the Deepwater Horizon disaster?
options: The water pressure at 5,000 feet crushed the device beyond its design limits
It had a dead battery and a faulty ram preventing it from activating
Operators accidentally disabled it during routine maintenance
